title: Replace octocrab with the existing generic tracker HTTP client
description:
Drop `octocrab` from the forge seam's native rung and issue the two GraphQL calls through the HTTP client this repo already owns.

**Payoff:** −31 crates, and it retires RUSTSEC-2023-0071 — an ignored *vulnerability* on a code path this binary cannot reach (see Evidence).

**Estimate:** half a day to a day. Most of it is test-harness rewiring, not the client.

## Why this is small

The entire `octocrab` surface in `crates/thegn-svc/src/forge/native.rs` is three things:

```rust
octocrab::OctocrabBuilder::new().personal_token(token).build()
client.graphql::<Value>(body)                                  // -> serde_json::Value
match error { Graphql | GitHub { source } | Service | Hyper }  // classify_error
```

Two GraphQL queries, both string constants in that file (`PR_LIST_QUERY` and the `pr_status` query). All three parsers — `parse_graphql_pr_list`, `parse_graphql_pr`, `parse_graphql_pr_status` — already operate on `serde_json::Value`, are pure, and are fixture-tested. The circuit breaker, the 20s per-request timeout, and `resolve_token` are our code too.

Nothing octocrab-shaped survives into our logic. It is a POST that returns JSON.

## The client already exists

`crates/thegn-svc/src/issue/http.rs` (937 lines) is exactly this: `TrackerHttpClient` / `TrackerHttpOperation` with a process-wide concurrency semaphore (`MAX_IN_FLIGHT = 8`), one absolute deadline per logical operation, connect/read-idle timeouts, and body-size caps (`MAX_BODY_BYTES`). It already backs Jira, Linear and Kaneo. Note `issue/github.rs` does not use octocrab at all — it drives `gh`.

One wrinkle: `forge/native.rs` is sync and uses `rt.block_on(...)` because the `Forge` trait is sync (`try_each_sync`). `issue/http.rs` is async. Either reuse it under the existing `block_on`, or lift the bounded-policy pieces into a shared helper — decide during implementation, but do not silently drop the concurrency budget or the deadline.

## Evidence: the `rsa` stack is never executed

`resolve_token` ([native.rs:27](http://native.rs:27)) is bearer-token only — `GH_TOKEN` → `GITHUB_TOKEN` → `gh auth token`. A grep for `jwt|app_id|private_key|installation|jsonwebtoken` across `forge/` and `thegn-core`'s forge modules returns **nothing**. There is no GitHub App, JWT, or installation auth anywhere in the tree.

So `jsonwebtoken`, `rsa`, `p256`, `p384`, `ecdsa`, `num-bigint-dig`, `pkcs1`, `pkcs8`, `sec1`, `primeorder`, `rfc6979`, `elliptic-curve`, `crypto-bigint`, `ff`, `group` and `simple_asn1` are compiled and linked but unreachable — and `deny.toml` waives RUSTSEC-2023-0071 (the `rsa` Marvin timing sidechannel) for exactly that dead code.

## Scope

* `crates/thegn-svc/src/forge/native.rs` — replace client construction, `graphql()`, and `classify_error`.
* `crates/thegn-svc/src/forge/native_regression_tests.rs` — currently mocks by handing octocrab a `tower::service_fn`. Rewire to a local test server; `axum` is already a dependency.
* `crates/thegn-svc/src/forge/native_global_connectivity_tests.rs` — check for the same coupling.
* Remove `octocrab` from `Cargo.toml` `[workspace.dependencies]` and `crates/thegn-svc/Cargo.toml`.
* Remove the RUSTSEC-2023-0071 ignore from `deny.toml`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `octocrab` absent from `Cargo.lock`.
- [ ] RUSTSEC-2023-0071 ignore deleted from `deny.toml`; `cargo deny check` exits 0.
- [ ] `pr_status` and `pr_list` behave identically against the existing fixtures — the three parsers should need **no** changes.
- [ ] Error classification still distinguishes retryable from terminal, so the `gh` fallback rung still engages on the same conditions (this is what <issue id="c3fc775c-eff0-425e-80a0-ce9e4eaeaeb4" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-622/handle-typed-native-graphql-failures-and-preserve-forge-fallback">THE-622</issue> established — do not regress it).
- [ ] Enterprise/foreign-origin host handling from <issue id="2bc6dcb7-daae-4dd8-b106-00dfdee92a83" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-621/prevent-native-github-requests-from-ignoring-enterprise-and-foreign">THE-621</issue> is preserved.
- [ ] The circuit breaker and the 20s timeout still work; a stalled TLS handshake must not block a caller longer than today.
- [ ] `cargo nextest run --workspace` green; `just lint` green.
- [ ] Closure re-measured and recorded in `docs/audits/dependency-audit-2026-09-15.md`.

## Out of scope

Do not touch the `gh` CLI rung — it is the fallback that makes this change safe, and the `forge-leak` ratchet fences where `gh` may be called.
